| Day 01 - Points #rstats
Nowt special. Just some points. DfT traffic count sites with size and colour reflecting average annual daily flow of all traffic.
Click points for a popup showing total motor vehicles.


Show the code
# data available for DfT website

maplibre(style = carto_style("positron")) |> 
  fly_to(center = c(-0.4045492, 50.9365654), zoom = 10) |> 
  add_circle_layer(source = dft,
                   id = "dft counts",
                   circle_color = interpolate(column = "all_motor_vehicles", 
                                              values = c(0, 10000, 95000), 
                                              stops = c(dft_color[[1]], 
                                                        dft_color[[2]], 
                                                        dft_color[[3]])),
                   circle_radius = interpolate(column = "all_motor_vehicles", 
                                               type = "linear",

                                                          30000, 50000, 70000, 
                                                          1e+05),

| Day 02 - Lines #rstats
Interactive {leaflet} ma showing section of Leeds roadnetwork with 3 separate variables colour-coded and offset (+2m, 0, -2m).
Zoom out to see Chichester. Hover over road segment to see highlight option.

tss_geographic_sf <- tss_min
tss_timings_sf <- tss_min

tss_geographic_sf <- tss_geographic_sf |> 
  st_set_crs(27700) |>  st_transform(crs = 4326)

| Day 03 - Polygons #rstats
Polygons can get lost on an interactive map of a large area. Highlight their location by creating a separate layer using their centroids. Use {leaflet} groupOptions("Area_markers", zoomLevels = 3:16) to make this layer disappear when zoomed in.
Zoom into polygons and click for popup or hover for tooltip.


Show the code
f <- read_sf("../30days2025/data/all_disabled_bays.shp")
f_centers <- f |> st_centroid() |> st_transform(crs = 4326)
f <- f |> st_transform(crs = 4326)

pal <- colorNumeric("Oranges", f$TYPEID)

leaflet() %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.DarkMatter, group = "Dark",
    options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.35)) %>% 
  # other layers to display here
  addPolygons(data = f,
              fillColor = pal(f$TYPEID),
              opacity = 1,
              stroke = TRUE,
              weight = 1,
              color = "white",
              label = paste0(f$TYPE),
              popup = paste0("TYPEID: ", f$TYPEID, "<br />",
                             "TYPE: ", f$TYPE, "<br />",
                             "LENGTH: ", f$LENGTH, "<br />",
                             "CAPACITY: ", f$CAPACITY
                             ),
              group = "Area") %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = f_centers,
                   color = "black",
                   weight = 1,
                   fillColor = "transparent",
                   group = "Area_markers",
                   options = pathOptions(interactive = FALSE),
                   ) %>%                  
  groupOptions("Area_markers", zoomLevels = 3:16) %>% 
  addFullscreenControl(position = "topleft", pseudoFullscreen = FALSE)

Introduction
30DayMapChallenge is a opportunity for geospatial data experts to showcase their skills with an entire month, November, dedicated to a different challenge per day.



Categories for 2025


This is my contribution in which I demonstrate proficiency in GIS - Earthlight amd QGIS - and R, the statistical programming language, and the following geospatial visualisation packages: leaflet, mapview, mapsf, tmap, and mapgl.
The code sections below are hidden by default but can be viewed to better understand the creation of maps in a reproducible environment.
Feel free to pan and zoom on the maps provided. Some have additonal outputs that will be revealed by hovering or clicking on elements.
Others are merely images as the data involved would be too much (or in the case of GIS products, there’s no way to create an interactive environment).
